reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: All 3 gates passed. Gate 1 skipped (missing-validation finding — the issue is an absent REVOKE, not a dead function). Gate 2 passes — attack vector is unauthenticated anon via PostgREST (untrusted; no trust_assumptions in scope). Gate 3 passes — supabase/migrations/ is explicitly in scope. Spec deviation confirmed: 0001_create_attendance_schema.sql:10 grants ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA attendance ... ON FUNCTIONS TO anon, and no corresponding REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTIONS FROM anon exists in any migration (fix migration 20260317000001 L90 revokes TABLES only). The only current attendance-schema function (record_attendance_by_card) has intentional explicit anon GRANT EXECUTE (L102), so no currently-exploitable path exists; however, any future function created in the attendance schema will automatically inherit ALL for anon via default privileges, allowing unauthenticated PostgREST /rpc/<function> calls. CONFIRMED_POTENTIAL because attack path requires a future function to be added without realising the default privilege applies.
